skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Guide agents through creating, validating, and cleaning isolated Git worktrees for parallel feature, review, and hotfix work.
skill.summary: Guides isolated Git worktree setup, validation, and cleanup for parallel development.
skill.author: Doyajin174

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and the documented ../worktrees sibling-directory convention. I found no prompt injection, hidden exfiltration intent, or covert code execution. The main residual risk is a recursive cleanup command that lacks explicit confirmation guidance.

remediation.issue: Recursive worktree deletion is shown without confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require git worktree list, path verification, and user confirmation before any recursive removal command is run.

remediation.issue: Manual directory deletion is presented as cleanup guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer git worktree remove and git worktree prune, and reserve manual deletion for verified stale directories only.

remediation.issue: Parent-relative paths may be copied into the wrong working directory.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to resolve and display the target path before creating, entering, or removing a worktree.

content.value_statement: Parallel Git work can mix branches and uncommitted changes. This skill guides safe worktree setup, checks, cleanup, and review workflows.
actual_capabilities: Recommends a sibling worktrees directory and clear naming scheme.
Provides commands for feature, review, and hotfix worktrees.
Lists Git checks to run before and after creation.
Explains cleanup with worktree removal, pruning, and branch deletion.
Troubleshoots common errors such as checked-out branches and missing refs.
limitations: Does not inspect repository state unless the agent runs Git commands.
Assumes Git and project dependency tools are installed.
Uses example paths and branch names that must be adjusted.
Includes cleanup commands that require review before execution.

use_cases.title: Start Isolated Feature Work
use_cases.description: Create a separate checkout for a new feature without disturbing the main working directory.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests Separately
use_cases.description: Open a review branch in its own worktree so tests and edits stay separate from active work.

use_cases.title: Apply Hotfixes Without Context Switching
use_cases.description: Create a hotfix worktree from the main branch while ongoing feature work remains untouched.

prompt_templates.title: Create My First Worktree
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one feature branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help me create a Git worktree for a feature named auth. Check my current Git state first and explain each command before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare A Review Worktree
prompt_templates.scenario: Separate checkout for reviewing a remote branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a review worktree for PR 123 from origin/feature/pr-123. Verify the branch exists and keep the review separate from my current work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Parallel Branch Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a plan for parallel worktrees for feature/api and hotfix/critical. Confirm naming, paths, and cleanup steps before any destructive command.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Worktrees
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my existing Git worktrees, identify stale entries, and propose safe cleanup steps. Ask before deleting directories or branches.

output_examples.input: I need a feature worktree for authentication work.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks repository status, confirms the target branch plan, selects a sibling worktree path, and reports the new isolated workspace.

output_examples.input: Prepare a pull request review environment.
output_examples.output: The assistant refreshes remote refs, creates a review worktree from the PR branch, and reports the active branch and remote source.
The assistant lists active worktrees, separates stale entries from active work, and asks for confirmation before removing any directory.

best_practices: Run git status and git worktree list before creating or removing worktrees.
Use one consistent sibling directory and descriptive branch names.
Prefer git worktree remove and prune before manual directory deletion.
anti_patterns: Deleting worktree directories without verifying the exact target path.
Trying to check out the same branch in multiple worktrees.
Installing dependencies before confirming the active worktree location.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps create and manage Git worktrees for isolated feature, review, hotfix, and experiment work.

faq.question: Does it make changes to my repository?
faq.answer: It can guide commands that create branches, add worktrees, install dependencies, or remove worktrees when approved.

faq.question: Why use a sibling worktrees directory?
faq.answer: A consistent sibling directory keeps extra checkouts organized and separate from the primary repository directory.

faq.question: Can it review pull requests?
faq.answer: It can prepare a separate worktree for a pull request branch so review and testing stay isolated.

faq.question: What should I verify before cleanup?
faq.answer: Verify the current directory, active worktree list, branch status, and exact path before removing anything.

faq.question: Does it replace Git knowledge?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured workflow, but users should still understand and approve repository commands.
